correctness.rationale: The Gram-sign criterion is reconstructed from dual facet normals. Cube coordinate reflections reduce exhaustively to origin-containing vertex sets. Exact rational enumeration checks every candidate in dimensions 3, 4, and 5 and finds no local-but-global failure; a dimension-six witness is checked by its exact inverse Gram matrix and by all 35 tetrahedral faces. The finite search is exhaustive rather than sampled.
risks: A software implementation error is mitigated by exact arithmetic, explicit normalization logic, published count agreement, and a separate closed-form witness matrix; independent validation remains unperformed.

value.rationale: The result gives the exact first dimension in which a natural local nonobtuseness condition stops forcing global nonobtuseness inside the literature-motivated class of binary simplices. It identifies a complete low-dimensional cutoff and a concrete separating witness, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or a routine recomputation.
risks: The theorem is finite-dimensional and binary-specific; it does not settle the general k-face conjecture or classify dimension-six counterexamples.
sources: arXiv:1512.02940 explicitly frames local k-face nonobtuseness as a structural program and singles out 0/1-simplices.
arXiv:1209.3875 and arXiv:1512.03483 establish binary nonobtuse simplices as a studied geometric/computational class.
